section_summary: This section contains State Department records filed under decimal file 894.403 (Fine Arts in Japan) spanning 1930 to 1937, consisting of despatches, letters, memoranda, telegrams, and cross-reference sheets. Early documents from 1930 focus on Count Makino's request through Ambassador William R. Castle, Jr. for information on the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts to guide municipal development and prevent eyesore monuments during the post-earthquake reconstruction of Tokyo. Later records document State Department introductions for the Misses Wyatt to study private Japanese art collections in 1937, extensive internal deliberations in 1935 regarding the proposed acquisition of Alexander G. Moslé's renowned collection of Japanese armor and sword furniture by the Smithsonian Institution, Japanese participation in the 1939 San Francisco Exposition art exhibit, and architectural studies by Mr. Boyce.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Castle reports that Count Makino requested full information on the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts to guide municipal development and prevent eyesore monuments in post-earthquake Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Castle reports Count Makino asked about the Commission of Fine Arts and municipal planning bodies amid undesirable monument schemes in Tokyo; recommends sending the despatch to Chairman Charles Moore for advice.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 104 from Ambassador W. R. Castle, Jr., Regarding Japanese Interest in the Commission of Fine Arts

subfiles.about: The Department of State transmits Ambassador Castle's despatch to Fine Arts Commission Chairman Charles Moore, requesting information and advice for Count Makino.
subfiles.summary: Wilbur Carr sends Charles Moore Castle's despatch 104 on Makino's request, noting Castle suggests a personal letter and replies should come via the Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Charles Moore Transmitting Ambassador Castle's Despatch

subfiles.about: The Department of State informs Ambassador Castle that his request concerning the Fine Arts Commission has been forwarded to Chairman Charles Moore.
subfiles.summary: Carr acknowledges Castle's despatch 104, encloses the letter to Charles Moore, and promises to relay Moore's reply.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Department of State to Ambassador W. R. Castle, Jr.

subfiles.about: Fine Arts Commission Chairman Charles Moore agrees to confer with Ambassador Castle upon his return to Washington regarding assistance to the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Charles Moore acknowledges Carr's May 16 letter and Castle's despatch and will discuss a response with Castle on his return.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles Moore to Assistant Secretary of State Wilbur J. Carr

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note recording a letter to the Treasury Department regarding a two-volume catalog of Japanese art addressed to Dr. Hornbeck.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: September 16, 1935 Treasury letter on a two-volume catalog of Japanese objets d'art offered to Hornbeck for the Library or Archives (093.941/76a).
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Two-Volume Catalog of Japanese Objets d'Art

subfiles.about: Walter Lichtenstein requests State Department assistance and introductions for the Misses Wyatt to view private art collections in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Walter Lichtenstein asks Hornbeck whether Tokyo private art collections such as Baron Iwasaki's are open to the Misses Wyatt, sailing August 5, and for introductions; historian Schmitt is recovering.
subfiles.title: Letter from Walter Lichtenstein to Stanley K. Hornbeck Regarding the Misses Wyatt

subfiles.about: Dr. Hornbeck writes Ambassador Grew requesting assistance for the Misses Wyatt during their visit to private art collections in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck asks Grew to assist the Misses Wyatt, sisters-in-law of Chicago banker Edward Brown, in viewing Baron Iwasaki's and other art collections, enclosing an introduction.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew

subfiles.about: Dr. Hornbeck encloses a letter of introduction for the Misses Wyatt to Ambassador Grew and suggests contacting Count Kabayama in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Lichtenstein serious, properly introduced students are usually welcomed, encloses an introduction to Grew recommending Count Kabayama, and is pleased Schmitt is recovering.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Walter Lichtenstein

subfiles.about: A formal letter of introduction for the Misses Wyatt addressed to Ambassador Grew, suggesting Count Kabayama facilitate access to art collections.
subfiles.summary: Introduction for the Misses Wyatt to Grew, suggesting Count Kabayama of Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai to arrange permits for private and official collections.
subfiles.title: Letter of Introduction for the Misses Wyatt Addressed to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew

subfiles.about: Edith F. Wyatt asks Dr. Hornbeck whether they should proceed with or cancel their sailing to Japan in light of current conditions.
subfiles.summary: Edith Wyatt telegraphs that they booked the Asama Maru for August 5 for four months' art study and asks urgently whether to cancel given conditions.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Edith F. Wyatt to Stanley K. Hornbeck Inquiring About Travel to Japan

subfiles.about: Dr. Hornbeck advises Edith F. Wyatt that the State Department is not advising against travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck telegraphs that on present information the Department is not advising against travel to Japan.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Edith F. Wyatt Regarding Travel Advice

subfiles.about: Walter Lichtenstein thanks Dr. Hornbeck for the letter of introduction provided to the Misses Wyatt.
subfiles.summary: Lichtenstein thanks Hornbeck for the letter and introduction to Grew; Schmitt sends regards.
subfiles.title: Letter from Walter Lichtenstein to Stanley K. Hornbeck Expressing Gratitude

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note regarding discussions with Langdon Warner on securing Japanese cooperation for an art exhibit at the 1939 San Francisco Exposition.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: October 1937 Ballantine memorandum on Langdon Warner's request for help obtaining Japanese cooperation for an art exhibit at the 1939 San Francisco Exposition.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Langdon Warner Conference on San Francisco Exposition Art Exhibit

subfiles.about: Mabel T. Boardman recommends that the Secretary of State explore acquiring Alexander Moslé's collection of Japanese arms and armor for the Smithsonian Institution.
subfiles.summary: Mabel Boardman urges the US to secure Alexander Moslé's large Japanese art collection, rich in arms and armor, for the Smithsonian, noting Frederic Delano's interest.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mabel T. Boardman to Stanley K. Hornbeck Proposing Acquisition of the Moslé Collection

subfiles.about: Dr. Hornbeck reluctantly declines to recommend Secretary of State intervention in acquiring the Moslé collection for the Smithsonian.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Boardman that after consulting experts he must abstain from enlisting the Secretary in Smithsonian acquisition of the Moslé collection, and suggests the National Museum.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Mabel T. Boardman Regarding the Moslé Collection (File Carbon)

subfiles.about: Department letterhead copy of Dr. Hornbeck's letter to Mabel T. Boardman regarding the Moslé collection.
subfiles.summary: Letterhead copy of Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Boardman declining to urge Smithsonian acquisition of Moslé's collection and suggesting the National Museum.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Mabel T. Boardman Regarding the Moslé Collection (Letterhead Copy)

subfiles.about: Dr. Hornbeck explains the administrative governance of the Smithsonian Institution and declines to urge State Department intervention in purchasing Moslé's collection.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Moslé for two catalog volumes, explains acquisitions rest with the Smithsonian Regents, says he cannot urge the Secretary to act, and asks what to do with Moslé's papers and portfolio.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé Regarding Proposed Smithsonian Acquisition

subfiles.about: Additional carbon copy of Dr. Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Mabel T. Boardman regarding the Moslé collection.
subfiles.summary: File carbon of Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Boardman declining Secretary of State involvement in buying Moslé's collection and suggesting the National Museum.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Mabel T. Boardman (Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: Faint carbon copy of Dr. Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Mabel T. Boardman.
subfiles.summary: Faint carbon of Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Boardman declining to recommend Smithsonian purchase of the Moslé collection.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Mabel T. Boardman (Faint Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: An internal filing slip marked with decimal file number 894.403.
subfiles.summary: Filing slip for decimal file 894.403 within the Moslé collection correspondence.
subfiles.title: Filing Slip for Decimal File 894.403

subfiles.about: Dr. Hornbeck agrees to meet Alexander G. Moslé in Washington on Saturday morning, February 16, 1935.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck agrees to meet Moslé Saturday morning, February 16, and asks him to telephone on arrival in Washington.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé Scheduling an Appointment

subfiles.about: Calling card / address slip of Alexander G. Moslé showing his New York address.
subfiles.summary: Calling card of Alexander Moslé, 5 East Sixty-sixth Street, New York, with notations to Hornbeck and file 894.403.
subfiles.title: Calling Card of Alexander G. Moslé

subfiles.about: An office message slip recording an appointment for Dr. Hornbeck to see Alexander G. Moslé at 10:00 AM on February 16, 1935.
subfiles.summary: Message slip of February 16, 1935, 9:05 AM, telling Hornbeck that Moslé will see him at 10:00.
subfiles.title: Office Message Slip Regarding Appointment with Alexander G. Moslé

subfiles.about: Eugene H. Dooman reports expert appraisals of the Moslé collection and advises against involving the Secretary of State in Smithsonian acquisition.
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports Lodge of the Freer Gallery and a dealer praised the Moslé collection as probably America's finest of its kind, but advised the Secretary not to become involved; draft letters attached.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Eugene H. Dooman on the Moslé Collection of Japanese Armor and Sword Furniture

subfiles.about: A cross-reference note recording personal letters sent by Dr. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé and Mabel T. Boardman.
subfiles.summary: Document file note of March 6, 1935 recording Hornbeck's personal letters to Moslé and Boardman on the Moslé collection.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Recording Letters to Alexander G. Moslé and Mabel T. Boardman

subfiles.about: Carbon copy of Dr. Hornbeck's letter explaining why the Secretary of State cannot initiate Smithsonian purchase of Moslé's collection.
subfiles.summary: Two-page file carbon of Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Moslé: Smithsonian acquisition policy rests with its Regents, he cannot urge the Secretary to act, and asks about returning Moslé's papers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé (Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: Department letterhead copy of Dr. Hornbeck's letter to Alexander G. Moslé regarding the Smithsonian Institution.
subfiles.summary: A two-page Department of State letterhead copy of Stanley K. Hornbeck's letter to Alexander G. Moslé dated March 6, 1935. Hornbeck expresses appreciation for Moslé's collection catalog but explains that the statutory Establishment of the Smithsonian Institution does not handle acquisitions, precluding intervention by the Secretary of State.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé (Letterhead Copy)

subfiles.about: A handwritten slip from Alexander G. Moslé requesting to call on Dr. Hornbeck to discuss his collection.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note from Moslé asking to call on Hornbeck to discuss his collection and papers; file 894.403.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Message from Alexander G. Moslé Requesting an Appointment

subfiles.about: Maxwell M. Hamilton acknowledges Moslé's letter and schedules a tentative meeting with Dr. Hornbeck for March 23, 1935.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton, in Hornbeck's absence, tentatively arranges for Moslé to meet Hornbeck Saturday, March 23 at 11:00 AM, with telephone confirmation requested.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Alexander G. Moslé Scheduling an Appointment

subfiles.about: Additional carbon copy of Dr. Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter declining to seek Smithsonian purchase of the Moslé collection.
subfiles.summary: An additional two-page carbon copy of Stanley K. Hornbeck's letter of March 6, 1935, to Alexander G. Moslé. The letter conveys the Department's position that acquisitions by the Smithsonian Institution are the exclusive domain of its Regents and declines secretarial intervention.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé (Additional Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: Carbon copy of Eugene H. Dooman's memorandum summarizing appraisals of the Moslé collection and advising against secretarial involvement.
subfiles.summary: Carbon of Dooman's March 6, 1935 memorandum: Lodge and a dealer praised the Moslé armor and sword furniture, and the Secretary should stay out of it.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Eugene H. Dooman on the Moslé Collection (Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: Further duplicate carbon copy of Dr. Stanley K. Hornbeck's letter to Alexander G. Moslé dated March 6, 1935.
subfiles.summary: A further duplicate two-page carbon copy of Dr. Stanley K. Hornbeck's letter to Alexander G. Moslé dated March 6, 1935. It explains the governance rules of the Smithsonian Institution and declines to urge secretarial action for acquiring the collection.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Alexander G. Moslé (Duplicate Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: Further duplicate carbon copy of Dr. Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Mabel T. Boardman.
subfiles.summary: Further carbon of Hornbeck's March 6, 1935 letter to Boardman declining to request Secretary of State intervention in acquiring Moslé's collection.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Mabel T. Boardman (Further Carbon Copy)

subfiles.about: W. T. Turner recommends filing papers without action regarding architectural and inventive studies in Japan by Mr. Boyce.
subfiles.summary: Turner recommends filing without action the correspondence on Mr. Boyce's studies of Japanese inventive activities and architecture, since an instruction might discourage other sources.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by W. T. Turner Regarding Studies on Japanese Architecture and Inventive Activities by Mr. Boyce
